title: Central point is the fixed point
name: central_point_is_the_fixed_point
doc: The central point s = 1 is the unique fixed point — the point BSD is about.

title: Root number squares to one
name: root_number_squares_to_one
doc: The root number is an involution's eigenvalue: w ∈ {1, −1} and w² = 1.

title: Root number one iff rank even
name: root_number_one_iff_rank_even
doc: THE PARITY EQUIVALENCE. w = (−1)^rank says: w = 1 exactly when the rank is even. Checked for ranks 0..7, both directions.

title: Parity is an involution
name: parity_is_an_involution
doc: The sign map is itself compatible with the involution: adding one to the rank flips it, and adding two returns it — parity is a ℤ/2 action, the same involution once more.

title: The coin is an involution
name: the_coin_is_an_involution
doc: PULLED, AND REFLECTED BACK. Applying the map twice returns the origin, for every digit: the black-hole side and the white-hole side are two orbits of ONE map, not two mechanisms.

title: The harmonic is the only fixed point
name: the_harmonic_is_the_only_fixed_point
doc: HARMONIC IS WHAT THE MAP LEAVES IN PLACE, and there is exactly one such digit. The fixed point is not chosen; it is computed by filtering the surface.

title: All that is not harmonic is moved
name: all_that_is_not_harmonic_is_moved
doc: EVERYTHING NOT HARMONIC IS MOVED. Eight of the nine digits are carried to the other side.

title: The sides are equal and exchanged
name: the_sides_are_equal_and_exchanged
proposition: below.length = above.length ∧ below.map σ = above.reverse ∧ above.map σ = below.reverse
doc: The first form of this said `∀ d ∈ below, σ d ∈ above` — membership as the PREDICATE — and the kernel reported it dependent on propext and Quot.sound. The axiom-freedom gate refused it, and the restatement is stronger for it: naming the image list says WHICH element goes where, not merely that each lands somewhere on the other side.

title: The coin is two sides and one edge
name: the_coin_is_two_sides_and_one_edge
proposition: digits.filter (fun d => d < σ d) = below ∧ digits.filter (fun d => σ d == d) = [5] ∧ digits.filter (fun d => σ d < d) = above ∧ below.length + above.length + 1 = digits.length
doc: The surface is exactly the two sides and the edge, and σ itself sorts it: the digits it carries upward are `below`, the one it leaves in place is the edge, the digits it carries downward are `above` — so the sides are computed from the map rather than typed beside it, and 4 + 4 + 1 is what the sorting leaves. (Was the count alone, which read the two typed lists back, 2026-09-14.)

title: Every bit of resistance drains
name: every_bit_of_resistance_drains
proposition: ∀ d ∈ digits, resistance d + resistance (σ d) = 0
doc: EVERY BIT OF RESISTANCE DRAINS. Resistance is ODD under the involution — r(σd) = −r(d) — so each orbit sums to exactly zero. Nothing is left over anywhere on the surface.

title: The harmonic carries no resistance
name: the_harmonic_carries_no_resistance
doc: The harmonic point is the one that never had any: at the fixed point the resistance is zero before any folding, which is what makes it the edge rather than a side.

title: The whole surface sums to zero
name: the_whole_surface_sums_to_zero
doc: AND THE WHOLE SURFACE DRAINS AT ONCE. Summed over every digit, resistance is zero — the two sides cancel exactly, which is the sentence's "measured to drain" as an arithmetic identity.

title: The drain is exact at every scale
name: the_drain_is_exact_at_every_scale
doc: The drain is not an approximation that improves with scale: it is exact at every multiple, because oddness is preserved by scaling. Checked at four magnitudes.

title: Verified at every point below the bound
name: verified_at_every_point_below_the_bound
doc: VERIFIED AT EVERY POINT A FINITE CHECK REACHES — a thousand cases, decided in the kernel.

title: And false at the bound
name: and_false_at_the_bound
doc: AND FALSE. The very next case refutes it.

title: Finite verification does not entail the universal
name: finite_verification_does_not_entail_the_universal
doc: So a finite verification does not entail the unbounded claim: here is a property verified at a thousand consecutive points whose universal statement is FALSE. This is the whole reason a `by decide` proof over a finite list is not a proof of a conjecture over an infinite domain.

title: A bigger bound proves no more
name: a_bigger_bound_proves_no_more
proposition: ((List.range 10).all (failsAt 10) = true ∧ failsAt 10 10 = false) ∧ ((List.range 100).all (failsAt 100) = true ∧ failsAt 100 100 = false) ∧ ((List.range 1000).all (failsAt 1000) = true ∧ failsAt 1000 1000 = false) ∧ ((List.range 2000).all (failsAt 2000) = true ∧ failsAt 2000 2000 = false)

title: What a finite check does establish
name: what_a_finite_check_does_establish
doc: What a finite check DOES establish, stated exactly: a counterexample cannot be below the bound. That is a real result and it is not the conjecture.

title: The clay files quantify over finite lists
name: the_clay_files_quantify_over_finite_lists
doc: The corpus's Clay-named theorems quantify over finite lists of this size — nine points for the Riemann functional equation, seven for BSD. Recorded as arithmetic so the scale is not rhetorical: a nine-element check is nine cases, and the set of non-trivial zeros of ζ is not nine.

title: Sigma preserves degree
name: sigma_preserves_degree
proposition: ∀ t ∈ middleTypes, (σ t).1 + (σ t).2 = t.1 + t.2
doc: σ preserves total degree — it acts WITHIN H^n, which is why it decomposes it.

title: Fixed type is p equals q
name: fixed_type_is_p_equals_q
doc: The unique fixed type in degree 2k is (k,k). Here k = 2.

title: Diagonal is fixed at every k
name: diagonal_is_fixed_at_every_k
doc: And it is the same in every even degree: (k,k) is fixed, everything else is swapped. Checked at k = 0, 1, 2, 3.

title: Involution fixes the diagonal
name: involution_fixes_the_diagonal
doc: The involution and its fixed diagonal, together.

title: Orbit sums to zero
name: orbit_sums_to_zero
proposition: {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (h : IsInvolution σ) (x : α) : odd f σ x + odd f σ (σ x) = 0
doc: THE ODD PART CANCELS OVER EVERY ORBIT. For any involution, any f, any point: the pair {x, σx} sums to exactly zero. This is the general form of "every bit of resistance drains", and the coin's version of it is this theorem at σ d = 10 − d.

title: Odd vanishes at a fixed point
name: odd_vanishes_at_a_fixed_point
proposition: {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (x : α) (hx : σ x = x) : odd f σ x = 0
doc: THE HARMONIC POINT CARRIES NOTHING. Wherever σ fixes a point, the odd part is zero there — no involution hypothesis is needed, only that this point is fixed.

title: EvenPart is symmetric
name: evenPart_is_symmetric
proposition: {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (h : IsInvolution σ) (x : α) : evenPart f σ (σ x) = evenPart f σ x
doc: THE EVEN PART IS WHAT SURVIVES THE REFLECTION — it takes the same value at x and at σx.

title: The split loses nothing
name: the_split_loses_nothing
proposition: {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (x : α) : evenPart f σ x + odd f σ x = 2 * f x
doc: AND THE TWO HALVES RECONSTRUCT THE WHOLE. Nothing is lost in the split, and this one needs no involution at all — it is true of the two parts as defined, for every σ.

title: The instance cancels over every orbit
name: the_instance_cancels_over_every_orbit
proposition: ∀ d ∈ carrier, (height d - height (σ d)) + (height (σ d) - height (σ (σ d))) = 0

title: The instance has one harmonic point
name: the_instance_has_one_harmonic_point

title: The instance splits without loss
name: the_instance_splits_without_loss
proposition: ∀ d ∈ carrier, (height d + height (σ d)) + (height d - height (σ d)) = 2 * height d

title: Reversal is an involution
name: reversal_is_an_involution
proposition: T (T navierStokes) = navierStokes ∧ T (T euler) = euler
doc: T² = id. Reversing time twice returns the equation, whatever the viscosity.

title: Euler is time reversible
name: euler_is_time_reversible
doc: Euler is invariant: every term transforms alike, so T fixes it.

title: Viscosity breaks time reversal
name: viscosity_breaks_time_reversal
proposition: T navierStokes ≠ navierStokes ∧ (T navierStokes).timeDerivative = navierStokes.timeDerivative ∧ (T navierStokes).convective = navierStokes.convective ∧ (T navierStokes).pressure = navierStokes.pressure ∧ (T navierStokes).viscous ≠ navierStokes.viscous
doc: Navier-Stokes is NOT invariant, and the viscous term is the only one that differs.

title: Fixed points are exactly the inviscid
name: fixed_points_are_exactly_the_inviscid
doc: Invariance holds exactly when ν = 0: the fixed points of T are the inviscid equations.

title: Fixed points are p and pspace
name: fixed_points_are_p_and_pspace
doc: The classes σ fixes are exactly those closed under complement. P and PSPACE are; the status of NP is the open question.

title: Np and conp are swapped
name: np_and_conp_are_swapped
proposition: σ NP = coNP ∧ σ coNP = NP
doc: σ swaps NP and coNP — they are complements by definition, not by theorem.

title: If np is fixed then np equals conp
name: if_np_is_fixed_then_np_equals_conp
doc: THE HONEST IMPLICATION — a real one, not a projection of its own hypothesis. σ NP reduces to coNP definitionally, so assuming σ NP = NP IS assuming coNP = NP, and the conclusion is that assumption symmetrised. Its antecedent is exactly what nobody has settled, which is why this is stated as an implication and not discharged.  (An earlier draft of this file wrote `∀ c, σ c = c → σ c = c`, which is `h → h`: the same hypothesis-projection that made the old wave-57 "theorems" worthless. Removed.)

title: P is closed under complement
name: p_is_closed_under_complement
doc: P is a fixed point of σ. This one is discharged, because P really is closed under complement — the model records a theorem, not an assumption.

title: Chi and genus are inverse
name: chi_and_genus_are_inverse
doc: The round trip is the identity: χ and g carry the same information.

title: Sphere has euler characteristic two
name: sphere_has_euler_characteristic_two
doc: The sphere: g = 0, χ = 2. This is the surface Poincaré's 3-dimensional analogue is about.

title: Torus has euler characteristic zero
name: torus_has_euler_characteristic_zero
doc: The torus is flat: g = 1, χ = 0 — the boundary between positive and negative curvature.

title: Double torus has chi minus two and rank four
name: double_torus_has_chi_minus_two_and_rank_four
doc: THIS CORPUS: genus 2, χ = −2, and rank H₁ = 2 − χ = 4 — the band count the census uses.

title: Homology rank is twice the genus
name: homology_rank_is_twice_the_genus
doc: rank H₁(Σ_g) = 2g, equivalently 2 − χ, at every genus checked.

title: Sigma is an involution
name: sigma_is_an_involution
doc: σ² = id. The functional equation's symmetry is an involution, exactly like every other σ in this corpus.

title: Critical line is the fixed point
name: critical_line_is_the_fixed_point
doc: The fixed point is n = 1, i.e. s = 1/2 — the critical line.

title: Sigma pairs the plane
name: sigma_pairs_the_plane
doc: σ pairs s with 1−s: the trivial-zero side and the far side reflect onto each other, s = 0 ↔ s = 1, s = −2 ↔ s = 4 (in halves: −1 ↔ 2).

title: The fixed line is one half
name: the_fixed_line_is_one_half
doc: Re(s) = 1/2 is the ONLY line σ fixes: doubling, 2·(1/2) = 1 = the fixed numerator.

title: Involution fixes the critical line
name: involution_fixes_the_critical_line
doc: The involution and its fixed point, together.

title: Light is the fixed point
name: light_is_the_fixed_point
proposition: ∀ v ∈ sample, same (add light v) light = true
doc: LIGHT IS THE FIXED POINT OF COMPOSITION. Add any velocity to c and the result is c again — not approximately, not in a limit: the same fraction, exactly, at every sample. This is the sense in which c is not a speed among speeds but the fixed point of the operation that combines them.

title: Light is fixed from either side
name: light_is_fixed_from_either_side
proposition: ∀ v ∈ sample, same (add v light) light = true
doc: And from the other side, because composition is not assumed commutative until it is checked.

title: Rest is the identity
name: rest_is_the_identity
proposition: ∀ v ∈ sample, same (add rest v) v = true
doc: REST IS THE IDENTITY. Adding nothing changes nothing — the other distinguished element.

title: Composition is symmetric
name: composition_is_symmetric
proposition: ∀ u ∈ sample, ∀ v ∈ sample, same (add u v) (add v u) = true
doc: COMPOSITION IS SYMMETRIC in the two velocities, at every pair of the sample.

title: Below c composes to below c
name: below_c_composes_to_below_c
proposition: ∀ u ∈ subluminal, ∀ v ∈ subluminal, (add u v).num < (add u v).den

title: The boost preserves the interval
name: the_boost_preserves_the_interval
proposition: ∀ e ∈ events, ∀ b ∈ boosts, interval (boostT b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) (boostX b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) = (b.2 * b.2 - b.1 * b.1) * interval e.1 e.2
doc: THE INTERVAL IS INVARIANT UP TO THE ONE COMMON FACTOR. For every event and every boost, the boosted interval equals the original times (q² − p²) — the same factor throughout, independent of the event, which is exactly what "the boost preserves the interval" means once denominators are cleared.

title: The light cone is carried to itself
name: the_light_cone_is_carried_to_itself
proposition: ∀ e ∈ lightlike, ∀ b ∈ boosts, interval (boostT b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) (boostX b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) = 0

title: The reverse boost undoes the boost
name: the_reverse_boost_undoes_the_boost
proposition: ∀ e ∈ events, ∀ b ∈ boosts, boostT (-b.1) b.2 (boostT b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) (boostX b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) = (b.2 * b.2 - b.1 * b.1) * e.1 ∧ boostX (-b.1) b.2 (boostT b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) (boostX b.1 b.2 e.1 e.2) = (b.2 * b.2 - b.1 * b.1) * e.2
doc: THE BOOST IS UNDONE BY THE REVERSE BOOST. Boosting by (p, q) and then by (−p, q) returns every event, scaled by the same common factor q² − p² the interval carries: with denominators cleared, the reverse boost IS the inverse, exactly, at every event and every boost — velocity and its negative (2026-09-14).

title: The reverse boost undoes every boost
name: the_reverse_boost_undoes_every_boost
proposition: ∀ p q t x : Int, boostT (-p) q (boostT p q t x) (boostX p q t x) = (q * q - p * p) * t ∧ boostX (-p) q (boostT p q t x) (boostX p q t x) = (q * q - p * p) * x
doc: …and for EVERY event and EVERY boost, proved rather than decided: the theorem above checks eight events under five boosts; this holds for all integers p, q, t, x at once. Multiplying out leaves q²t − qpx + pqx − p²t, and the cross terms cancel because multiplication commutes. A proof, not an exhaustion — it rests on the standard axioms propext and Quot.sound that core's integer lemmas carry.

title: Sq lt
name: sq_lt
proposition: (a b : Int) (hl : -b < a) (hr : a < b) : a*a < b*b
tactic: have hp : 0 < (b - a) * (b + a) := Int.mul_pos (by omega) (by omega)
doc: Strictly inside the band (−b, b) means a strictly smaller square.

title: Lt of sq
name: lt_of_sq
proposition: (a b : Int) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a*a < b*b) : -b < a ∧ a < b
doc: A smaller square (with b positive) means inside the band.

title: Interval scales
name: interval_scales
proposition: (p q t x : Int) : interval (boostT p q t x) (boostX p q t x) = (q*q - p*p) * interval t x
doc: For every event and every boost the interval is multiplied by q² − p², and by nothing else.

title: Scale positive
name: scale_positive
proposition: (p q : Int) (h : belowC p q) : 0 < q*q - p*p
doc: Below c that factor is positive.

title: Timelike invariant
name: timelike_invariant
proposition: (p q t x : Int) (h : belowC p q) (ht : 0 < interval t x) : 0 < interval (boostT p q t x) (boostX p q t x)
tactic: have hs := scale_positive p q h
doc: TIMELIKE STAYS TIMELIKE in every frame below c.

title: Spacelike invariant
name: spacelike_invariant
proposition: (p q t x : Int) (h : belowC p q) (ht : interval t x < 0) : interval (boostT p q t x) (boostX p q t x) < 0
tactic: have hs := scale_positive p q h
doc: SPACELIKE STAYS SPACELIKE: no boost makes a spacelike separation reachable.

title: Null invariant
name: null_invariant
proposition: (p q t x : Int) (ht : interval t x = 0) : interval (boostT p q t x) (boostX p q t x) = 0
doc: The light cone is frame-independent: null in one frame is null in all.

title: Timelike order absolute
name: timelike_order_absolute
proposition: (p q t x : Int) (h : belowC p q) (hfuture : 0 < t) (hcausal : x*x ≤ t*t) : 0 < boostT p q t x
doc: FOR A CAUSAL SEPARATION EVERY OBSERVER BELOW c AGREES WHICH EVENT CAME FIRST. The closed cone: the null case |x| = t is in, because a light signal carries causation too.

title: Spacelike order reverses
name: spacelike_order_reverses
proposition: (t x : Int) (ht : 0 < t) (hx : t < x) : belowC (2*t+1) (2*x) ∧ boostT (2*t+1) (2*x) t x = -x
tactic: refine ⟨⟨by omega, by omega, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
doc: FOR A SPACELIKE SEPARATION THERE IS A FRAME BELOW c IN WHICH THE ORDER REVERSES — exhibited: with 0 < t < x, the boost β = (2t+1)/(2x) sends Δt to −x.

title: Spacelike simultaneous
name: spacelike_simultaneous
proposition: (t x : Int) (ht : 0 < t) (hx : t < x) : belowC t x ∧ boostT t x t x = 0
tactic: refine ⟨⟨by omega, by omega, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
doc: …and a frame in which the two events are simultaneous: β = t/x sends Δt to 0.

title: Velocity addition below c
name: velocity_addition_below_c
proposition: (p₁ q₁ p₂ q₂ : Int) (h₁ : belowC p₁ q₁) (h₂ : belowC p₂ q₂) : belowC (addNum p₁ q₁ p₂ q₂) (addDen p₁ q₁ p₂ q₂)
tactic: obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := h₁; obtain ⟨d, e, f⟩ := h₂
doc: TWO BOOSTS BELOW c COMPOSE TO A BOOST BELOW c, for every pair — c is not approached by adding.

title: Closure is one hundred sixty two
name: closure_is_one_hundred_sixty_two
doc: The closure has exactly rows x cols cells: 18 x 9 = 162 for the installed library.

title: Closure is the product
name: closure_is_the_product
doc: The product law, at several shapes — the size is rows x cols and not an accident of 18 and 10.

title: Closure has no duplicate
name: closure_has_no_duplicate
doc: NO CELL IS REPEATED. This is the bijection, and it is strictly stronger than "every pair is present": a list carrying one pair twice and omitting another would satisfy presence at the right length, and would still have a hole in it.

title: Address inverts
name: address_inverts
proposition: ∀ p ∈ cells 18 9, row 9 (idx 9 p.1 p.2) = p.1 ∧ col 9 (idx 9 p.1 p.2) = p.2
doc: THE ADDRESS INVERTS. Row-major indexing recovers both coordinates for every cell, so a scene can be addressed by one number without losing which geometry and which material it names.

title: Addresses are the interval
name: addresses_are_the_interval
doc: The addresses are exactly 0 … 179, each used once: the closure is an interval, not a scatter.

title: The compound fraction clears
name: the_compound_fraction_clears
doc: The clearing itself: FOCAL/(FOCAL - z) = 24/(24 - k) reduces to 12 * 10 = 5 * 24.

title: Focal plane is unit scale
name: focal_plane_is_unit_scale
doc: AT THE FOCAL PLANE THE SCALE IS UNITY. z = 0 gives 24/24 = 1: objects on the plane through the origin are neither enlarged nor reduced, which is what makes FOCAL a focal length.

title: Depth is strictly monotone
name: depth_is_strictly_monotone
doc: NEARER ENLARGES, FURTHER RECEDES, STRICTLY. For depths inside the focal point, k1 < k2 implies 24/(24-k1) < 24/(24-k2), stated by cross-multiplication so no division occurs. This is the monotonicity the TS fold checks numerically and the property two canvas painters violated by faking depth as a screen offset before the 2026-07-07 audit.

title: Frustum brackets the focal plane
name: frustum_brackets_the_focal_plane
doc: The frustum the camera declares is non-degenerate: near < FOCAL < far, in tenths, with the depth planes half a lattice pitch either side of the focal plane (near 19/10, far 29/10).

title: Denominator is positive on the frustum
name: denominator_is_positive_on_the_frustum
doc: The projection never divides by zero on the declared frustum: the denominator stays positive for every depth between the near and far planes.

title: Reflection is an involution
name: reflection_is_an_involution
doc: σ² = id on every cell of the closure.

title: Reflection closes on the closure
name: reflection_closes_on_the_closure
doc: σ maps the closure onto itself — the symmetry does not leave the space.

title: Reflection has no fixed point
name: reflection_has_no_fixed_point
doc: NO cell is its own reflection. ONE even side is enough: a fixed cell would need g = rows−1−g AND m = cols−1−m, so an even side makes its own coordinate unfixable and the conjunction fails whatever the other side does. The closure is 18 x 9 — the columns ARE odd, and m = 4 is fixed — yet no CELL is, because 18 is even. Both sides odd is the only case with a fixed point, exactly as the digit reflection d ↦ 10 − d fixes 5 and nothing else.

title: The closure is eighty one orbits
name: the_closure_is_eighty_one_orbits
doc: So the closure is 81 orbits of two, with nothing left over.

title: Orbit positions cancel
name: orbit_positions_cancel
doc: THE ORBITS SUM TO ZERO. Each pair of reflected cells cancels in both coordinates, exactly — the involution law this corpus states everywhere, holding here because the lattice is centred.

title: Reflection complements the address
name: reflection_complements_the_address
doc: ROW-MAJOR REFLECTION IS ADDRESS COMPLEMENT: idx(σ c) + idx(c) = 179, for all 180 cells. The geometric symmetry and the arithmetic one are the same symmetry, which is not visible from either the layout or the addressing alone.

title: The involution laws are general
name: the_involution_laws_are_general
proposition: (reflIsInvolutive 8 8 = true) ∧ (reflStaysInside 8 8 = true) ∧ (reflComplementsAddress 8 8 = true) ∧ (orbitPositionsCancel 8 8 = true) ∧ (reflIsInvolutive 3 3 = true) ∧ (reflComplementsAddress 3 3 = true) ∧ (orbitPositionsCancel 3 3 = true) ∧ -- ONE even side suffices, and only both-odd fails: 18x9 and 9x18 have no fixed cell, 3x3 does. (reflHasNoFixedPoint 8 8 = true) ∧ (reflHasNoFixedPoint 9 18 = true) ∧ (reflHasNoFixedPoint 3 3 = false) ∧ (reflHasNoFixedPoint 5 7 = false)
doc: The same four laws at other shapes, so none of them is an accident of 18 and 10. Both sides odd breaks the no-fixed-point law and only that one — 3×3 has a centre cell that is its own reflection — while involutivity, closure, cancellation and complement survive everywhere.

title: Middle forms have dimension six
name: middle_forms_have_dimension_six
doc: dim Λ²(ℝ⁴) = 6 — the middle degree in four dimensions, where ★ maps 2-forms to 2-forms.

title: Selfdual and antiselfdual split the six
name: selfdual_and_antiselfdual_split_the_six
doc: The split: self-dual ⊕ anti-self-dual, 3 + 3 = 6. This is why four dimensions are special — only there does ★ map middle forms to middle forms.

title: Star is an endomorphism only in the middle
name: star_is_an_endomorphism_only_in_the_middle
doc: ★ sends Λ^k to Λ^(n−k), so it is an ENDOMORPHISM exactly when k = n − k. At n = 4 that holds for k = 2 and fails for k = 1, which is why the self-dual split is a statement about 2-forms in four dimensions and not about forms in general.

title: Involution splits the middle forms
name: involution_splits_the_middle_forms
doc: The involution and the split it produces, together.

title: Euler characteristic and genus are inverse
name: euler_characteristic_and_genus_are_inverse
proposition: (∀ g ∈ List.range 10, genusOf (chi g) = g ∧ 2 - chi g = 2 * (g : Int)) ∧ eulerChi = chi 2 ∧ homologyLoops = 2 - chi 2
doc: χ and the genus are INVERSE: reading the genus back from χ(g) returns g for every surface up to genus 9, and rank H₁ = 2 − χ = 2g at each one. The corpus's own surface is the instance g = 2 — eulerChi is χ(2) and homologyLoops is 2 − χ(2) — derived by the law, not typed beside it.

title: The genus reads back from chi at every genus
name: the_genus_reads_back_from_chi_at_every_genus
doc: …and at EVERY genus, proved rather than decided: the theorem above checks the first ten surfaces; this reads the genus back from χ(g) for all of them at once. A proof, not an exhaustion — it rests on the standard axioms propext and Quot.sound that core's integer lemmas carry, and the axiom probe reports it as general.

title: Census bands are gapless and descending
name: census_bands_are_gapless_and_descending
proposition: fib 10 = 55 ∧ fib 9 = 34 ∧ fib 8 = 21 ∧ fib 7 = 13 ∧ fib 10 = fib 9 + fib 8 ∧ fib 9 = fib 8 + fib 7
doc: The band ladder: `homologyLoops` consecutive Fibonacci terms descending from F(10).

title: Census is one hundred twenty three
name: census_is_one_hundred_twenty_three
proposition: fib 7 + fib 8 + fib 9 + fib 10 = 123 ∧ fib 12 - fib 8 = 123
doc: UNFOLDED_CENSUS = ΣF(7..10) = 123, and the same by the closed form F(12) − F(8).

title: Fibonacci partial sum identity
name: fibonacci_partial_sum_identity
proposition: (fib 1 + fib 2 + fib 3 + fib 4 + fib 5 = fib 7 - fib 2) ∧ (fib 3 + fib 4 + fib 5 + fib 6 + fib 7 + fib 8 = fib 10 - fib 4) ∧ (fib 7 + fib 8 + fib 9 + fib 10 = fib 12 - fib 8) ∧ (fib 2 + fib 3 + fib 4 + fib 5 + fib 6 + fib 7 + fib 8 + fib 9 + fib 10 + fib 11 = fib 13 - fib 3)
doc: Σ_{i=a}^{b} F(i) = F(b+2) − F(a+1), at five windows — the census is an instance of a theorem, not a coincidence at one window.

title: Folding by chi is undone by unfolding
name: folding_by_chi_is_undone_by_unfolding
proposition: (∀ n ∈ List.range 200, ((n : Int) + eulerChi) - eulerChi = n) ∧ ((fib 7 + fib 8 + fib 9 + fib 10 : Nat) : Int) + eulerChi = 121
doc: Folding by χ and unfolding by −χ are inverse at every count below 200, and the folded census is the unfolded one folded: ΣF(7..10) + χ = 121, with the unfolded census recomputed from fib.

title: Reflection is an involution
name: reflection_is_an_involution
proposition: reflect (reflect 1) = 1 ∧ reflect (reflect 2) = 2 ∧ reflect (reflect 3) = 3 ∧ reflect (reflect 4) = 4 ∧ reflect (reflect 5) = 5 ∧ reflect (reflect 6) = 6 ∧ reflect (reflect 7) = 7 ∧ reflect (reflect 8) = 8 ∧ reflect (reflect 9) = 9
doc: r is an involution on 1…9: r(r(d)) = d for every nonzero digit.

title: Reflection pairs and one fixed point
name: reflection_pairs_and_one_fixed_point
doc: The pairs 1↔9, 2↔8, 3↔7, 4↔6 and the single fixed point 5↔5.

title: Reflection closes on the digits
name: reflection_closes_on_the_digits
doc: r maps the nonzero digits INTO the nonzero digits. At base 11 it would not: r(1) = 10.

title: Reflection is an involution on the whole lattice
name: reflection_is_an_involution_on_the_whole_lattice
proposition: ∀ d ∈ List.range (digitLattice + 1), reflect (reflect d) = d ∧ d + reflect d = digitLattice
doc: The reflection is an involution on the WHOLE lattice 0…10, and every pair sums to it: the ten is the constant the involution preserves, not a number asserted beside it.

title: Golden ratio bounds
name: golden_ratio_bounds
doc: `φ ≈ 1.618` as an exact two-sided bound on a Fibonacci ratio: F(n+1)/F(n) → φ.

title: Golden ratio minus one bounds
name: golden_ratio_minus_one_bounds
doc: `φ − 1 ≈ 0.618` — the same statement one octave down, since φ − 1 = 1/φ and F(n−1)/F(n) → 1/φ. Stated as a two-sided bound, NOT as a disjunction: a disjunction here would be satisfiable by either half and so would assert almost nothing.

title: Splitting then burning water is the identity
name: splitting_then_burning_water_is_the_identity
proposition: (∀ e ∈ List.range 1000, burnHydrogen (splitWater e) = e) ∧ (∀ mol ∈ [1, 10, 1000, 1000000], burnHydrogen (splitWater (mol * bondTenths)) = mol * bondTenths)
doc: σ² = id on the energy ledger: burning what was split returns the starting energy exactly, at every ledger value below 1000 and at every molar scale. The round trip holds whatever the bond is, so the typed enthalpy is data and the law is the claim.

title: Verify beats recompute by magnitudes
name: verify_beats_recompute_by_magnitudes
doc: To trust a result conventionally you re-run it, O(N); a Merkle receipt is verified along one path of depth log₂ N. Cited from uuidna's Cipher.lean, address 5040eb7c.

title: Hexbit receipt beats rebuild
name: hexbit_receipt_beats_rebuild
doc: A full binary tree over 2^n leaves costs 2^n − 1 merges to rebuild; a receipt costs n, one per line of the hexagram. Stated at four rungs, INCLUDING the rung where there is no advantage at all: at n = 1 both cost 1, so the claim is bounded from below by its own counterexample.

title: Hexbit advantage widens
name: hexbit_advantage_widens
doc: The gap WIDENS: (2^n − 1)/n is increasing, checked as a cross-multiplied integer inequality so no division and no rounding enters the statement.

title: Shor state vectors unchanged
name: shor_state_vectors_unchanged
doc: The three state vectors the simulation materialises: 2^(t+w) amplitudes for (t,w) = (8,4), (10,5), (12,6). This is the resource the honesty claim is ABOUT, and it is unchanged by any loop that skips terms equal to zero.

title: Shor vector dwarfs the number
name: shor_vector_dwarfs_the_number
doc: Each vector dwarfs the number it factors by more than a hundredfold — the exponential a physical device would not spend, stated as three inequalities.

title: Shor rsa gap is between exponents
name: shor_rsa_gap_is_between_exponents
doc: RSA is out of reach by an inequality between EXPONENTS, not by a shortage of patience: a 2048-bit modulus needs ~2^(3·2048) amplitudes against the 2^60 that already exhausts addressable memory.

title: Shor zero skipping divides by the work register
name: shor_zero_skipping_divides_by_the_work_register
doc: Visiting only the non-zero amplitudes divides the inner-loop count by the work-register size W exactly, because the oracle writes one entry per x: dense W·T², sparse T². An exact factor, so the speedup claim is arithmetic and not a benchmark.

title: Gi add re
name: gi_add_re
doc: The parts of a sum, a product and the literals 0 and 1 — what a proof over ALL matrices unfolds to. Stated at the file's own namespace so the inventory names each one.

title: Gi mul re
name: gi_mul_re
proposition: (x y : GI) : (x * y).re = x.re * y.re - x.im * y.im

title: H unitary
name: h_unitary
doc: HADAMARD IS UNITARY UP TO ITS RECORDED SCALE: H · H† = 2 · I.

title: H squared
name: h_squared
doc: Hadamard twice is twice the identity — it undoes itself, with the same factor 2.

title: Paulis unitary
name: paulis_unitary
proposition: Same 2 (mm 2 X (dag X)) idm ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 Z (dag Z)) idm ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 S (dag S)) idm
doc: X, Z and S are unitary: U · U† = I.

title: Y unitary
name: y_unitary
proposition: Same 2 (mm 2 Y (dag Y)) idm ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 Y Y) idm
doc: Y is unitary and its own inverse, like the other Paulis.

title: S squared
name: s_squared
doc: S squared is Z.

title: Cnot
name: cnot
proposition: Same 4 (mm 4 CNOT (dag CNOT)) idm ∧ Same 4 (mm 4 CNOT CNOT) idm
doc: CNOT is unitary and its own inverse.

title: Swap
name: swap
proposition: Same 4 (mm 4 SWAP (dag SWAP)) idm ∧ Same 4 (mm 4 SWAP SWAP) idm
doc: SWAP is unitary and its own inverse.

title: Toffoli
name: toffoli
proposition: Same 8 (mm 8 TOFFOLI (dag TOFFOLI)) idm ∧ Same 8 (mm 8 TOFFOLI TOFFOLI) idm
doc: Toffoli is unitary and its own inverse.

title: Omega fourth
name: omega_fourth
doc: ω really is a primitive eighth root: ω⁴ = −1, so ω⁸ = 1 and no smaller power is.

title: T gate
name: t_gate
proposition: SameW (mmW TW (dagW TW)) idW ∧ SameW (powW TW 8) idW ∧ ¬ SameW (powW TW 4) idW ∧ ¬ SameW (mmW HW TW) (mmW TW HW)
doc: T IS UNITARY, HAS ORDER EXACTLY 8 (T⁸ = I, T⁴ ≠ I), AND DOES NOT COMMUTE WITH HADAMARD.

title: Bell state
name: bell_state
doc: THE BELL STATE IS SUPPORTED ON EXACTLY 00 AND 11, WITH EQUAL WEIGHT.

title: Ghz state
name: ghz_state
doc: The GHZ state is supported on exactly 000 and 111, with equal weight.

title: Chsh classical bound
name: chsh_classical_bound
proposition: ∀ a0 a1 b0 b1 : Bool, chshClassical a0 a1 b0 b1 = 2 ∨ chshClassical a0 a1 b0 b1 = -2
doc: EVERY ASSIGNMENT OF DEFINITE VALUES GIVES |S| = 2 — the classical bound, all sixteen cases.

title: Chsh quantum value
name: chsh_quantum_value
doc: THE BELL STATE BREAKS THE BOUND: the scaled sum is 8 = S · ⟨Φ|Φ⟩ · √2, so S² = 8² / (2² · 2) = 8, beyond the classical 2² = 4.

title: Teleport exact
name: teleport_exact
proposition: ∀ b, b < 2 → ∀ r, r < 8 → teleport b r = if r % 2 = b then 1 else 0
doc: EVERY OUTCOME OF QUBITS 0 AND 1 LEAVES QUBIT 2 HOLDING THE INPUT, with equal weight.

title: Teleport no signalling
name: teleport_no_signalling
proposition: ∀ s, s < 6 → reduced2 (sentFrom (pauliEigen s)) 0 1 = 0 ∧ reduced2 (sentFrom (pauliEigen s)) 1 0 = 0 ∧ reduced2 (sentFrom (pauliEigen s)) 0 0 = reduced2 (sentFrom (pauliEigen s)) 1 1
doc: NO SIGNALLING: before the corrections, qubit 2 alone is the same for every Pauli eigenstate input — off-diagonals zero, diagonals equal.

title: Superdense exact
name: superdense_exact
proposition: ∀ m, m < 4 → ∀ r, r < 4 → (superdense m r ≠ 0 ↔ r = m)
doc: EACH OF THE FOUR MESSAGES DECODES TO EXACTLY ITS OWN BASIS STATE: one qubit carries two bits.

title: Both ways
name: both_ways
proposition: (∀ m, m < 4 → ∀ r, r < 4 → (superdense m r ≠ 0 ↔ r = m)) ∧ ∀ b, b < 2 → ∀ r, r < 8 → teleport b r = if r % 2 = b then 1 else 0
doc: Both directions over one pair: one qubit carries two classical bits, and two carry one qubit.

title: No cloning
name: no_cloning
proposition: (u : Mat) (h0 : ∀ r, r < 4 → ap 4 u (basis 0) r = basis 0 r) (h2 : ∀ r, r < 4 → ap 4 u (basis 2) r = basis 3 r) : ap 4 u (fun r => basis 0 r + basis 2 r) 1 ≠ 1
doc: NO LINEAR MAP THAT COPIES |0⟩ AND |1⟩ COPIES |+⟩: its image of |+⟩|0⟩ is not |+⟩|+⟩.

title: Cnot copies the basis
name: cnot_copies_the_basis
proposition: (∀ r, r < 4 → ap 4 CNOT (basis 0) r = basis 0 r) ∧ (∀ r, r < 4 → ap 4 CNOT (basis 2) r = basis 3 r)
doc: The hypotheses are not vacuous: CNOT is such a map — it copies the basis states exactly.

title: Stabilizer hadamard
name: stabilizer_hadamard
proposition: Exact (kron 2 H idm) ruleH0 2 ∧ Exact (kron 2 idm H) ruleH1 2
doc: H ON EITHER QUBIT ACTS ON EVERY PAULI STRING AS ITS RULE SAYS (times its recorded factor 2).

title: Stabilizer phase
name: stabilizer_phase
proposition: Exact (kron 2 S idm) ruleS0 1 ∧ Exact (kron 2 idm S) ruleS1 1
doc: S on either qubit acts on every Pauli string as its rule says.

title: Stabilizer cnot
name: stabilizer_cnot
doc: CNOT acts on every Pauli string as its rule says.

title: Deutsch jozsa
name: deutsch_jozsa
proposition: ∀ f, f < 16 → (constant f = true → (dj f 0).normSq = 16) ∧ (balanced f = true → dj f 0 = 0)
doc: ONE QUERY DECIDES: a constant function leaves all weight on 00, a balanced one leaves none.

title: Promise census
name: promise_census
doc: The promise is not empty on either side: two functions are constant and six are balanced.

title: Grover search
name: grover_search
proposition: ∀ m, m < 4 → ∀ r, r < 4 → (grover m r ≠ 0 ↔ r = m)
doc: ONE GROVER ITERATION OVER FOUR ITEMS LEAVES ALL WEIGHT ON THE MARKED ITEM.

title: Qft unitary
name: qft_unitary
proposition: ∀ j, j < 8 → ∀ k, k < 8 → sum8 (fun i => qft j i * iqft i k) = if j = k then 8 else 0
doc: THE TRANSFORM IS UNITARY UP TO ITS RECORDED SCALE: QFT · QFT† = 8 · I.

title: Phase estimation exact
name: phase_estimation_exact
proposition: ∀ k, k < 8 → ∀ r, r < 8 → sum8 (fun j => iqft r j * wPow (j * k)) = if r = k then 8 else 0
doc: PHASE ESTIMATION IS EXACT ON AN EIGENPHASE k/8: the inverse transform returns |k⟩.

title: Swap routing
name: swap_routing
doc: ROUTING PRESERVES THE FUNCTION: SWAP(0,1) · CNOT(1,2) · SWAP(0,1) is exactly CNOT(0,2).

title: Unrouted differs
name: unrouted_differs
doc: And the routing is needed: the unrouted neighbour gate is a different function.

title: Routed depth
name: routed_depth
proposition: (d : Nat) (h : 1 ≤ d) : routedGates d = 2 * d - 1 ∧ routedGates 2 = 3
doc: A routed CNOT at distance d ≥ 1 takes 2d − 1 gates; at distance 2, the three above.

title: Repetition corrects
name: repetition_corrects
proposition: ∀ b : Bool, ∀ e, e < 4 → decode (flip e (encode b)) = b
doc: THE REPETITION CODE CORRECTS EVERY SINGLE BIT FLIP, and no flip at all.

title: Repetition fails on two
name: repetition_fails_on_two
doc: AND IT DOES NOT CORRECT TWO: the claim above is sharp, not vacuous.

title: Steane corrects
name: steane_corrects
doc: EACH SINGLE-QUBIT ERROR TRIPS ITS OWN NONZERO SYNDROME — the position it names.

title: Steane css
name: steane_css
proposition: ∀ a, a < 3 → ∀ b, b < 3 → ((List.range 7).filter fun i => hamming a i && hamming b i).length % 2 = 0
doc: Steane is CSS: every pair of checks overlaps on an even number of qubits.

title: Shor nine
name: shor_nine
proposition: (∀ a, a < 9 → flags bitChecks a ≠ flags bitChecks 9 ∧ ∀ b, b < 9 → flags bitChecks a = flags bitChecks b → a = b) ∧ ∀ a, a < 9 → flags phaseChecks a ≠ flags phaseChecks 9 ∧ ∀ b, b < 9 → (flags phaseChecks a = flags phaseChecks b ↔ a / 3 = b / 3)
doc: EVERY SINGLE BIT FLIP TRIPS ITS OWN SYNDROME, AND EVERY SINGLE PHASE FLIP NAMES ITS BLOCK.

title: Distance corrects
name: distance_corrects
proposition: (d t e₁ e₂ : Nat) (h : 2 * t + 1 ≤ d) (h₁ : e₁ ≤ t) (h₂ : e₂ ≤ t) : e₁ + e₂ < d
doc: At distance d ≥ 2t + 1, two error patterns of weight at most t never span d.

title: Pauli products
name: pauli_products
proposition: Same 2 (mm 2 X Y) (smul GI.i Z) ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 Y Z) (smul GI.i X) ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 Z X) (smul GI.i Y)
doc: THE PAULIS MULTIPLY CYCLICALLY WITH THE FACTOR i: XY = iZ, YZ = iX, ZX = iY.

title: Pauli anticommute
name: pauli_anticommute
proposition: Same 2 (mm 2 Y X) (smul (-GI.i) Z) ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 Z Y) (smul (-GI.i) X) ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 X Z) (smul (-GI.i) Y)
doc: Reversed, each product changes sign — so distinct Paulis anticommute and commute to 2i times the third.

title: Pauli square adjoint trace
name: pauli_square_adjoint_trace
proposition: (Same 2 (mm 2 X X) idm ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 Y Y) idm ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 Z Z) idm) ∧ (Same 2 (dag X) X ∧ Same 2 (dag Y) Y ∧ Same 2 (dag Z) Z) ∧ (tr2 X = 0 ∧ tr2 Y = 0 ∧ tr2 Z = 0 ∧ tr2 idm = 2)
doc: Each Pauli squares to the identity, is its own adjoint, and has trace zero.

title: Hadamard exchanges phase and bit
name: hadamard_exchanges_phase_and_bit
proposition: Same 2 (mm 2 (mm 2 H Z) H) (smul 2 X) ∧ Same 2 (mm 2 (mm 2 H X) H) (smul 2 Z)
doc: HADAMARD EXCHANGES THE PHASE FLIP AND THE BIT FLIP: H·Z·H = 2·X and H·X·H = 2·Z — the reason the phase-flip code is the bit-flip code read in the Hadamard basis.

title: Ghz mermin quantum
name: ghz_mermin_quantum
proposition: ∀ r, r < 8 → ap 8 xxx ghz r = ghz r ∧ ap 8 xyy ghz r = -(ghz r) ∧ ap 8 yxy ghz r = -(ghz r) ∧ ap 8 yyx ghz r = -(ghz r)
doc: GHZ IS A +1 EIGENSTATE OF XXX AND A −1 EIGENSTATE OF XYY, YXY AND YYX.

title: Ghz mermin classical
name: ghz_mermin_classical
proposition: ∀ x1 x2 x3 y1 y2 y3 : Bool, ¬ (pm x1 * pm x2 * pm x3 = 1 ∧ pm x1 * pm y2 * pm y3 = -1 ∧ pm y1 * pm x2 * pm y3 = -1 ∧ pm y1 * pm y2 * pm x3 = -1)
doc: NO DEFINITE VALUES REPRODUCE THOSE FOUR SIGNS: all sixty-four assignments fail — the product of the three −1 lines is x₁x₂x₃ again, so it would have to be both −1 and +1.

title: No communication
name: no_communication
proposition: ∀ k, k < 7 → bobDensity (aliceDoes k) 0 1 = 0 ∧ bobDensity (aliceDoes k) 1 0 = 0 ∧ bobDensity (aliceDoes k) 0 0 = bobDensity (aliceDoes k) 1 1
doc: BOB'S HALF IS MAXIMALLY MIXED WHATEVER ALICE DOES: off-diagonals zero, diagonals equal, for all seven.

title: Alice changes the pair
name: alice_changes_the_pair
doc: The claim is not empty: Alice's operation does change the pair — only Bob's half cannot tell.

title: Toll is uniform
name: toll_is_uniform
proposition: ∀ s, s < 6 → ∀ m, m < 4 → tollWeight (pauliEigen s) m = tollWeight (pauliEigen s) 0 ∧ tollWeight (pauliEigen s) 0 ≠ 0
doc: THE FOUR OUTCOMES CARRY EQUAL WEIGHT FOR EVERY PAULI EIGENSTATE: the two classical bits say nothing about what crosses.

title: Entanglement swapping
name: entanglement_swapping
proposition: ∀ m, m < 4 → outerDet (swapped bell bell) m ≠ 0 ∧ (outer (swapped bell bell) m 0 0).normSq = (outer (swapped bell bell) m 1 1).normSq ∧ (outer (swapped bell bell) m 0 1).normSq = (outer (swapped bell bell) m 1 0).normSq
doc: TWO QUBITS THAT NEVER MET ARE LEFT ENTANGLED ON EVERY OUTCOME: nonzero determinant, and the two amplitudes that survive have equal weight.

title: No pairs no swapping
name: no_pairs_no_swapping
doc: And it is the pairs' entanglement that is swapped: from product pairs the outer two stay a product.

title: Sixty degrees is a primitive sixth root of unity
name: sixty_degrees_is_a_primitive_sixth_root_of_unity
proposition: EI.ω * EI.ω = EI.ω + -1 ∧ EI.pow EI.ω 3 = -1 ∧ EI.pow EI.ω 6 = 1 ∧ (List.range' 1 5).all (fun k => EI.pow EI.ω k != 1)
doc: SIXTY DEGREES IS A PRIMITIVE SIXTH ROOT: ω² = ω − 1, ω³ = −1, ω⁶ = 1 and no smaller power is 1.

title: Rotation by sixty degrees keeps the eisenstein integers
name: rotation_by_sixty_degrees_keeps_the_eisenstein_integers
doc: ROTATING BY SIXTY DEGREES KEEPS ℤ[ω] IN ℤ[ω] — for EVERY element, with integer coordinates and no halves.

title: The rotation leaves the integers and keeps the norm
name: the_rotation_leaves_the_integers_and_keeps_the_norm
proposition: EI.ω * 1 = EI.ω ∧ (EI.ω * 1).b ≠ 0 ∧ (List.range 5).all (fun a => (List.range 5).all (fun b => EI.norm (EI.ω * ⟨(a : Int) - 2, (b : Int) - 2⟩) == EI.norm ⟨(a : Int) - 2, (b : Int) - 2⟩)) ∧ (List.range 6).all (fun k => EI.norm (EI.pow EI.ω k) == 1)
doc: BUT NOT IN ℤ: the rotation of 1 is ω itself, which is no ordinary integer — the pasted claim's own list held 3/2 and −7/2, which are the real parts of exactly such elements. The norm is kept and is multiplicative on a box.

title: Six is the first perfect number and a tetrahedron sums to 720
name: six_is_the_first_perfect_number_and_a_tetrahedron_sums_to_720

title: The doubling circuit steps forty eighty one sixty and back
name: the_doubling_circuit_steps_forty_eighty_one_sixty_and_back
doc: THE DOUBLING CIRCUIT STEPS +40, +80, +160, −40, −80, −160 AND CLOSES; 3·6·9 IS EQUILATERAL AT 120.

title: The six two star is the two triangles and not the doubling cycle
name: the_six_two_star_is_the_two_triangles_and_not_the_doubling_cycle
proposition: [1, stepThree 1, stepThree (stepThree 1), stepThree (stepThree (stepThree 1))] = [1, 4, 7, 1] ∧ [2, stepThree 2, stepThree (stepThree 2), stepThree (stepThree (stepThree 2))] = [2, 5, 8, 2] ∧ circuit.length = 6 ∧ turn 1 4 = 120 ∧ turn 1 2 ≠ turn 2 4

title: The two reflections connect the three trinities
name: the_two_reflections_connect_the_three_trinities
proposition: digits.all (fun d => nines (nines d) == d && tens (tens d) == d) ∧ digits.filter (fun d => nines d == d) = [9] ∧ digits.filter (fun d => tens d == d) = [5] ∧ [3, 6, 9].map nines = [6, 3, 9] ∧ [1, 4, 7].map nines = [8, 5, 2] ∧ [3, 6, 9].map tens = [7, 4, 1] ∧ [2, 5, 8].map tens = [8, 5, 2] ∧ digits.all (fun d => trinity (nines d) == (3 - trinity d) % 3) ∧ digits.all (fun d => trinity (tens d) == (4 - trinity d) % 3)
doc: BOTH ARE INVOLUTIONS WITH ONE FIXED DIGIT EACH (9 and 5). THE NINES' REFLECTION KEEPS 3·6·9 AND EXCHANGES 1·4·7 WITH 2·5·8; THE TENS' REFLECTION EXCHANGES 3·6·9 WITH 7·4·1 AND KEEPS 2·5·8.

title: The two mirrors compose to the forty degree step
name: the_two_mirrors_compose_to_the_forty_degree_step
proposition: digits.all (fun d => next d == d % 9 + 1) ∧ digits.all (fun d => (angle (nines d) + angle d) % 360 == 0) ∧ digits.all (fun d => (angle (tens d) + angle d) % 360 == 40) ∧ digits.all (fun d => iter next 9 d == d) ∧ (List.range' 1 8).all (fun k => iter next k 1 != 1) ∧ digits.all (fun d => trinity (next d) == (trinity d + 1) % 3) ∧ ((List.range 9).map (fun k => digits.map (iter next k)) ++ (List.range 9).map (fun k => digits.map (fun d => iter next k (nines d)))).eraseDups.length = 18

title: The nines reflection carries the doubling circuit onto itself
name: the_nines_reflection_carries_the_doubling_circuit_onto_itself
proposition: circuit.map nines = [8, 7, 5, 1, 2, 4] ∧ circuit.all (fun d => nines (2 * d % 9) == 2 * nines d % 9) ∧ circuit.map tens = [9, 8, 6, 2, 3, 5]
doc: THE NINES' REFLECTION COMMUTES WITH DOUBLING, so it carries the circuit onto itself, half a turn round.

title: A two to one fold of addresses is many to one by pigeonhole
name: a_two_to_one_fold_of_addresses_is_many_to_one_by_pigeonhole
doc: TWO ADDRESSES IN, ONE OUT: 256 bits fold to at most 122 free, so the fold is many-to-one by pigeonhole — on average 2^134 pairs to an address. A count, not an attack.

title: Add comm sample
name: add_comm_sample
doc: Addition commutes — checked on representatives, not inherited from a library.

title: Add assoc sample
name: add_assoc_sample
doc: Addition associates.

title: Mul comm sample
name: mul_comm_sample
doc: Multiplication commutes.

name: exact_addition
doc: 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6, exactly — no floating point anywhere in the corpus's arithmetic.

title: Amplitude normalisation
name: amplitude_normalisation
doc: Amplitude normalisation |α|² + |β|² = 1, exactly, on the 3-4-5 triple: (3/5)² + (4/5)² = 1. The old file stated this with a hypothesis of the same shape as its conclusion; here the amplitudes are given and the identity is checked.

title: Amplitude normalisation rational
name: amplitude_normalisation_rational
doc: The same, as rationals: 9/25 + 16/25 = 1.

title: Sothic cycle meshes
name: sothic_cycle_meshes
doc: The Sothic cycle meshes the Egyptian civil year — 1461 × 365 = 1460 × 365.25, in whole quarter-days.

name: graeco_latin_order_five
proposition: (latin 5 a5 && latin 5 b5 && orthogonal 5 a5 b5) = true

proposition: [2, 3, 5].all (fun p => (List.range 12).all (fun m => (List.range 12).all (fun n => vp p 64 (choose' (m + n) n) == carries p 16 m n 0))) = true

title: Tau six is product
name: tau_six_is_product
doc: 0·counter — τ(6) = τ(2)·τ(3): the stated values multiply (−24)(252) = −6048. Instances, not Hecke's law.

title: K5 k33 break planar bounds
name: k5_k33_break_planar_bounds
doc: 0·forward — K₅ and K₃,₃ break the planar bounds e ≤ 3v−6 and (bipartite) e ≤ 2v−4.

title: Steiner two three seven
name: steiner_two_three_seven
proposition: (List.range 7).all (fun a => (List.range 7).all (fun b => a == b || covers a b == 1)) = true

title: Heawood moore bound
name: heawood_moore_bound
